tasks.spec:
You are fixing ONE bookkeeping defect in the master timeline derivation in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally or publish. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth only, zero API spend. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp for everything you run.

FILES YOU OWN: server/pipeline/av_sync.py and tests/test_av_sync.py. You may regenerate /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/timeline.json.

DO NOT REBUILD THE STEMS. The four files in episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/stems/ have ALREADY been independently verified correct by the coordinator and must not be deleted, overwritten or re-encoded. Measured on them: the guest's audio stem reads exactly 0.00 energy at 30s, 120s and 184.7s (he joins at 224.65s); his video stem reads luma 0.98 there against 96.73 when his camera is on; the host's 76.86s mic dropout reads 0.00 energy inside against 108 before and 749 after; the host's audio at raw second 2000 lands at grid 2078s against an expected 2077s with correlation peak 0.993; and the host's video frames 164 seconds apart inside his 203.9s camera dropout differ by 0.00 while a live frame differs by 20.01. Your work is a JSON regeneration, not a render. If you find yourself invoking ffmpeg to encode, you have gone out of scope.

THE DEFECT. Your previous pass added _probe_track in server/pipeline/av_sync.py, which backfills a packet whose ffprobe duration_time is N/A with the delta to the NEXT packet. That is a defensible reading, and the code comment about Daily's late-join camera first frame spanning 1.419 seconds is accurate. But it makes dropout detection depend on whether ffprobe happened to report a duration, which is a container metadata artifact rather than a property of the recording. On these files both camera tracks carry exactly 41 duration-less packets as a leading prefix. Under the current rule, ANY real dropout that happens to follow a duration-less packet is silently absorbed into that packet's span and disappears from the timeline entirely. That is precisely the failure this master-timeline stage exists to make impossible, because the timeline is the authoritative record of where each track was actually producing data. The concrete symptom today: the guest camera opens at 224.896s, emits one frame, then produces nothing until 226.315s, and timeline.json records ZERO dropouts for guest_video.

THE FIX. Make hole derivation UNIFORM across every packet, ignoring reported durations entirely for this purpose. For each track compute a nominal step as the MEDIAN packet-to-packet delta (median, not mean, so a 203-second dropout cannot drag it), then report a hole wherever `pts[i] - pts[i-1] - nominal > 0.4`, recording it at `pts[i-1] + nominal` with that duration. Apply this to audio and video alike. Keep everything else about the timeline as it is; first_pts_s, last_pts_s, grid_offset_s, container_start_s and filename_epoch_offset_s are all already correct and independently confirmed.

EXPECTED RESULT after the change, independently derived by the coordinator from the raw packets. Your regenerated timeline.json must land within about 0.05s of these:
  host_audio   nominal 0.0200s   1 hole    76.860s total, the big one at 151.859s
  host_video   nominal 0.0330s  13 holes  219.960s total, the big one at  25.713s for 203.887s
  guest_audio  nominal 0.0200s   0 holes     0.000s total
  guest_video  nominal 0.0320s   1 hole      1.387s total, at 224.928s
Note host_video moves from 220.376s to about 219.960s: that is expected and correct, because each gap is now measured against the real 33ms frame interval instead of the container's nominal 1ms tick. guest_video moves from 0 holes to 1. If you cannot reproduce these numbers, your derivation still disagrees with the packets and you should fix that rather than adjust anything.

TESTS. Add a regression test to tests/test_av_sync.py, using a synthetic packet list and no media, that FAILS under the old rule and passes under the new one: a long gap immediately following a packet whose duration_time is N/A must be reported as a hole rather than absorbed into that packet's span. Add a second test pinning that the nominal step is the median so a single enormous dropout does not inflate it and mask smaller ones. Keep every existing test unless the change genuinely invalidates one; if so, replace its guarantee and explain in the docstring why the old failure mode cannot recur. Never delete a regression test without replacing it.

THE RECEIPT you must satisfy, and should run yourself:
  python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/podcast-full-auto/stems_check.py
It re-derives every timeline number from the raw packets using exactly the uniform rule described above, so a hand-edited timeline.json will not survive it, and it then re-verifies all four stems end to end. It takes several minutes because it decodes the stems.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real terminal output into your final message: the receipt command above, and `cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_av_sync.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty; the coordinator reviews and lands it.
tasks.verified: timeline.json records every dropout under one uniform packet-delta rule that cannot be defeated by a missing container duration, matches an independent re-derivation from the raw packets, and all four already-verified stems still pass end to end
